transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-26 16:00 PST | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Patel, Carlos Mendez, Asha Rao, Ben Turner, Sofia

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. quick intro — Jordan Lee, AE.
00:08 Carlos Mendez: Hi Jordan, Carlos here, CTO at Mariner Tech. we got a small team on, thanks for doing this.
00:12 Priya Patel: Hi, Priya SE. today we'll run through the hosted API for chat and text, streaming, how to tune params, and common retry patterns. we'll also show a quick view of the Console and Optimize suggestions.
00:25 Asha Rao: Awesome. high level, we're trying to add a chat assistant to our customer portal. main concerns: latency under 400ms p95, cost per call, and data residency.
00:36 Jordan Lee: Great, that's helpful. quick qual — are you currently using any LLM APIs?
00:39 Ben Turner: We're prototyping with OpenAI right now. doing a lot of small calls, but costs spiking. also running some inference in house but ops overhead is big.
00:48 Priya Patel: Totally. with Redwood hosted API we try to give predictable pricing and streaming so perceived latency is lower. i'll demo streaming first — so the API can stream tokens as they're generated, which improves UX for chat.
01:05 Priya Patel: (screen share) here's an example curl and JS snippet. you open a streaming connection, we send chunked events with partial deltas, you can render as they arrive. common gotcha: front-end should support re-assembly of chunks and handle reconnects.
01:22 Sofia: can we do streaming in websockets as well?
01:24 Priya Patel: yep, websocket and SSE supported. SSE is often easiest for browser clients.
01:30 Carlos Mendez: what's the p99 latency for streaming vs non-streaming?
01:33 Priya Patel: good question. streaming reduces time-to-first-token significantly — usually 100-300ms improvement depending on model and prompt length. tail latency depends on sequence length and batching; we provide model profiles in the Console so you can pick variants.
01:50 Jordan Lee: Also worth noting batching and KV cache can reduce token cost when you have repeated prefixes, e.g., system prompts or long histories.
01:58 Asha Rao: about params — what do you recommend for temperature, top_p, and max_tokens for helpful but concise answers?
02:04 Priya Patel: we usually recommend temperature 0.0-0.3 for deterministic system replies, 0.6-0.8 for creative. max_tokens depends on expected response size — we enforce both prompt + completion token limits. also show stop sequences if you need structured outputs.
02:20 Ben Turner: and retries — we had issues with duplicate charges when retrying on the client side with OpenAI. how do you handle idempotency and retries?
02:28 Priya Patel: Redwood supports idempotency keys for create requests. if you resend the same idempotency key within the window, the service returns the same result and won't double bill. we also provide recommended client-side retry logic: exponential backoff with jitter, retry on 5xx or networking errors, but not on 4xx that indicate bad request.
02:48 Carlos Mendez: is there a default window for idempotency?
02:51 Priya Patel: default is 5 minutes, but for Dedicated/Private deployments we can extend that.
02:58 Jordan Lee: And we store audit logs for requests, with optional redaction; security docs cover retention and KMS integration.
03:05 Asha Rao: can you briefly show the Console where we can see cost per route?
03:10 Priya Patel: yeah, switching — Console dashboard. here's per-route token breakdown, per-model latency percentiles, and Optimize suggestions which will recommend batching and quantization profiles for your workload.
03:28 Sofia: the Optimize suggestions look handy, is that automated?
03:31 Priya Patel: it's automated by analyzing call patterns and offering a small set of changes with estimated cost savings. you can preview the potential impact before applying.
03:40 Ben Turner: on PII concerns: we need SOC2 and SSO. do you support SAML/SSO and do you have SOC2 cert?
03:47 Jordan Lee: yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC supported; we are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO compliance docs. i'll email the security packet after the call.
03:55 Carlos Mendez: great. for latency — we need p95 under 400ms for short chats (<= 100 tokens). is that feasible on hosted?
04:02 Priya Patel: for short responses and the right model variant and region selection we can hit p95s in the 200-350ms range. if you need tighter guarantees we recommend Dedicated. also smart routing can fall back to lower-latency variants.
04:18 Asha Rao: about costs: can we see an example cost calc?
04:20 Jordan Lee: yes I'll include a pricing sheet with per-token and per-embedding numbers and an example calc based on your expected QPS.
04:29 Priya Patel: quick demo of retry pattern in code — here's pseudo-code for exponential backoff with jitter, and using an idempotency key. note: do not retry on 4xx.
04:45 Ben Turner: any guidance on concurrency limits? we may have 200 QPS bursts.
04:49 Priya Patel: for hosted you can request rate limit increases; for sustained high QPS we recommend Dedicated where you get reserved capacity and predictable throughput. for the POC you can also burst.
05:02 Carlos Mendez: we might want to try a POC for a month. what's the onboarding like?
05:06 Jordan Lee: quick self-serve API key to start in minutes, we can provision trial credits, and then we do a short scoping call with Priya to define POC success metrics.
05:15 Sofia: any sample prompt templates for customer support?
05:18 Priya Patel: yes, we'll share a repo of templates and a short evaluation harness to capture metrics like helpfulness and hallucination rate.
05:28 (background noise)
05:35 Jordan Lee: ok quick recap of action items and next steps. Jordan to send pricing and SOC2 packet, Priya to send streaming and retry code samples and the templates repo, Ben to share expected traffic numbers and whitelisted IPs, and we'll schedule a POC scoping meeting.
05:54 Carlos Mendez: sounds good, thanks everyone.
05:57 Priya Patel: thanks, we'll follow up.
06:01 End meeting.
